children: Indian government bonds are likely to extend losses on Monday, as hawkish comments from Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh have pushed up expectations of a U.S. interest rate hike as early as next month.

The yield on the benchmark 6.94% 2036 bond (IN069436G=CC) is expected to trade between 6.90% and 6.94%, a trader at a private bank said, after closing at 6.9108%, the highest since June 11, in the previous session.
"Bearish factors globally are putting relentless pressure on bonds, making the task of protecting yield levels all the more tough for bulls," the trader said.

U.S. Treasury yields jumped on Friday, led by the interest rate sensitive two-year yield, after Warsh said the central bank would "have work to do" if policymakers were not confident inflation was returning to its 2% target, fueling bets on a September rate hike.

The comments, made at the Fed’s annual Jackson Hole symposium, acknowledged that financial conditions do not appear restrictive and were Warsh's clearest indication yet that further rate hikes may be needed to curb inflation.
Fed funds futures are now pricing in 60% odds of a hike in September, up from 35% before Warsh's comments.

The benchmark Brent crude contract rose above $90 per barrel in Asian trading, after U.S. forces struck two rocket launchers on Iran's Larak Island on Sunday, marking the first known American strikes on the Islamic republic since late July.
Elevated crude prices affect major energy importers such as India, as expensive oil fuels inflation and strains the current account and government finances.
The minutes of the Reserve Bank of India's August monetary policy showed policymakers were open to raising rates if inflation risks materialise.
India's overnight indexed swap rates are expected to jump in line with bond yields.
On Friday, the one-year (INR1YMIBROIS=CC) swap rose 3 bps to 5.95%, while the two-year (INR2YMIBROIS=CC) rate advanced to 6.1325%. The five-year (INR5YMIBROIS=CC) rates settled at 6.4375%.
